div.head: Ine 57
div.ab: CI. Gif ciorl ceap forsteleþ ⁊ byrð into his huse (vel ærne), ⁊ hit mon ðærinnne befehð, þonne bið his dæl scyldig buton þam wife anum, forðon heo sceal hire hlaforde hyran: gif heo dear mid aþe gecyþan ðæt heo þæs forstolenan ne onbite, nime hire ðriddan gescead.

CI. Gif ceorl ceap forstilð ⁊ bireð into his ærne, ⁊ befehð þærinne mon, þonne bið se his dǽl synnig butan þam wife anum, forðon hio sceal hire ealdore hieran: gif hio dear mid aðe gecyðan, þæt hio þæs forstolenan ne onbite, nime hire ðriddan sceat.

Si ceorl aliquod captale furetur et deferat in suum ærne ([deorne] id est secretum habitaculum suum), et intercipiatur ibi, sit sue parti reus preter feminam eius solam, quia ipsa debet domino suo parere: si audeat iureiurando satisfacere, quod de ipso furto non gustauit, habeat (ipsa) suam terciam partem pecunie.

{CI} Gif ceorl ceap forstilð ⁊ bireð into his ærne, ⁊ befehð þærinne mon, þonne bið se his dǽl synnig butan þam wife anum, forðon hio sceal hire ealdore hieran. Gif hio dear mid aðe gecyðan, þæt hio þæs forstolenan ne onbite, nime hire ðriddan sceat.

If a ceorl steals property and takes it into his house, and it is caught therein, then he is liable for his portion [of the household goods]; only his wife is exempted, because she must obey her superior. If she dare declare on oath, that she did not partake of the stolen goods, let her take her third portion [of the household goods].

If a husband steals a beast and carries it into his house, and it is seized therein, he shall forfeit his share [of the household property] — his wife only being exempt, since she must obey her lord. If she dare declare, with an oath, that she has not tasted the stolen [meat], she shall retain her third of the [household] property.

If a husband steals any cattle and brings it into his house, and it is seized therein, he is guilty for his part, but without his wife, for she must obey her lord; if she dare declare with an oath that she did not taste of the stolen meat, she is to receive her third portion.

Wenn ein Ehemann Fahrhabe stiehlt und in sein Haus bringt, und man ertappt (es) darin, dann ist jener für seinen Theil [zwar] schuldig, nur ohne die Ehefrau, weil sie ihrem Eheherrn gehorchen soll: wenn sie durch Eid zu beweisen wagt, dass sie von dem Gestohlenen nicht genoss, nehme sie ihren dritten Heller (des Haushaltsvermögens).

If a husband steals movable goods and brings them into his house, and (they) are seized there, then he is [indeed] guilty for his share, but not his wife, because she must obey her lord: if she dares to prove by oath that she did not partake of the stolen goods, let her take her third penny (of the household property).
